name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

11	
12	`DivFamZarAff.mapAlg` (`…AffMapAlg.lean`) base-changes the widened class along an algebra
13	**tower instance pack** `[Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']`.  That is the right form
14	whenever a tower is already in scope, and it is what the S5b Zariski keystones are stated at.
15	
16	It is **not** the form the divisor vehicle consumes.  `divFamZar`
17	(`DivisorFamilyZarVehicle.lean`) indexes its compatibility condition by the section-restriction
18	maps `Over.resAlgHom T h`, which are bare `AlgHom`s carrying no tower instance, so the vehicle
19	and hence `divFunctor` are stated entirely at `DivFamZar.mapAlgHom`.  Until the widened carrier
20	has that same face, a widened class exists only at an affine test and nothing carries it to a
21	general one — measured at HEAD: outside the `DivisorFamilyAff*` files the name `DivFamZarAff`
22	appeared nowhere in the tree.
23	
24	So this file is the missing half of the base-change layer, and it is deliberately a *verbatim*
25	transcription of the chart-typed one: same names modulo `Aff`, same statements, same proofs.
26	Nothing here is new mathematics — `mapAlgHom` is `mapAlg` at `RingHom.toAlgebra` of the map,
27	and the two functor laws come from `mapAlg_id` / `mapAlg_comp` at the induced towers.  The
28	value of writing it is that the *consumer* side becomes typeable at all.
29	
30	## Why `[IsProper C.hom]` appears here and not in the chart-typed file
31	
32	`DivFamZarAff.mapAlg` needs it (`…AffMapAlg.lean` §Transport): properness is what makes
33	`AffCoverData.HasAffineOverlaps` free, and the widened certificate transport needs overlap
34	affineness because an arbitrary affine open's overlaps are not affine by fiat the way basic
35	opens of a fixed affine chart were.  It is a hypothesis the DD-R lane carries everywhere, so
36	this costs no generality — but it is stated rather than hidden, since it is exactly one of the
37	things I-0492 clause 4(ii) warns the old typing was silently supplying.
38	
39	## Main declarations
40	
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom` — the explicit-map face.
42	* `DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_id`, `mapAlgHom_comp` — the functor laws on that face.
43	* `DivFamZarAff.mapAlg_congr`, `mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg` — the face-change bridge, so a statement
44	  proved at a tower can be consumed at a restriction map and conversely.
45	* `DivFamZarAff.picClass_mapAlgHom` — the Abel hook on that face.
46	* `DivFamZarAff.congr` — transport along an isomorphism of test algebras.

10	
11	`divFamZarAff_of_forall_prime_certified_adaptation` (`…AffAssemble.lean`) is the endpoint of
12	the widened certificate lane, and what it returns is a class **at an affine test**
13	`DivFamZarAff C R n`.  Every DD-R consumer is stated against a *functor* on the whole slice
14	over `Spec k`, so between the lane's endpoint and its consumers sits the affine-opens limit —
15	the `divFamZar` vehicle of `DivisorFamilyZarVehicle.lean` — and that layer had no widened
16	counterpart.  This file supplies it, following the chart-typed template line for line.
17	
18	## The shape, and why it is unchanged by R2
19	
20	A section over a test `T` is a family of widened classes, one per affine open of `T.left`,
21	compatible under restriction.  R2 widened where the pieces live **on the curve**; it changed
22	nothing about the Zariski structure of the **base**.  So the vehicle's shape is literally the
23	old one with `DivFamZar` replaced by `DivFamZarAff` and `mapAlgHom` by the widened face of
24	`…AffFace.lean` — which is precisely why that face had to exist first.
25	
26	`[IsProper C.hom]` is carried throughout: the widened base change needs it (an arbitrary affine
27	open's overlaps are not affine by fiat), and it is a hypothesis the DD-R lane has everywhere.
28	
29	## What this file does NOT do, stated precisely
30	
31	It defines the widened vehicle and proves its affine collapse.  It does **not** define the
32	restriction `divFamZarAff.map` along an arbitrary morphism of test objects, and therefore does
33	not define the widened *functor* either.  That is the remaining item of the R2 lane

11	**The pinned keystone, ported to the widened carrier** (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2 at

13	`R` glue to a widened class over `R` restricting to them.
14	
15	## Why this ports, and where the only real work was
16	
17	R2 (human decision I-0492) widened where the certificate's pieces live ON THE CURVE — arbitrary
18	affine opens instead of basic opens of two pinned `P¹` charts.  It changed NOTHING about the
19	Zariski cover of the BASE, and the gluing argument is entirely about the base: it assembles a
20	divisor with `awayGluedEquationsLoc` and witnesses local certifiability by `mapAlg` of the input
21	families.  So the route below is the chart-typed `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat` with three
22	mechanical substitutions — `DivFamZar → DivFamZarAff`, `CertifiedDivisorFamily →
23	CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff`, and no `π` anywhere — plus two real costs:
24	
25	* the assembly had to be **restated at bare local-equation systems** first, because its
26	  chart-typed statement demands `CertifiedDivisorFamily` input that a widened class provably
27	  cannot supply.  That is `DivisorFamilyAffGlueZarKit.lean`; the proof there is verbatim.
28	* every `CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.mapAlg` carries the overlap-affineness argument `hinf`, free
29	  here from `[IsProper C.hom]` via `AffCoverData.hasAffineOverlaps_of_isProper`, which is also
30	  what `DivFamZarAff.mapAlg` itself needs.  Hence `[IsProper C.hom]` in the statement — the DD-R
31	  lane has it everywhere, the challenge curve being proper over `k`.
32	
33	## The route, unchanged from the chart-typed keystone
34	
35	Representatives `d i` carry widened local certificate covers `h i : Fin (m i) → S i` with
36	certified families `G i l` over `Localization.Away (h i l)`.  The composite cover
37	`r ⟨i, l⟩ := a i l * g i` (numerators `a i l` of the `h i l`, `IsLocalization.Away.sec`) spans `⊤`
38	(`span_range_num_mul_eq_top`), and the fine carriers `Localization.Away (h i l)` are
39	`r ⟨i, l⟩`-away localizations of `R`.  The fine overlap carriers receive the coarse overlap
40	carriers `T i j` by `IsLocalization.Away.lift`; the fine compatibility follows from the class-level
41	compatibility pulled to the fine overlaps through the two factorizations of each comparison.  The
42	widened certified-input gluing core produces the glued class, and the restriction law at the
43	coarse level follows by Zariski separation (`DivFamZarAff.eq_of_away_eq`) over each `S i` against
44	its fine cover.

9	/-!
10	# The Zariski divisor assembly, freed of the certificate carrier (R2 keystone kit)
11	
12	The S5 divisor assembly of `DivisorFamilyZariskiGlue.lean` — `awayGluedEquations` and its
13	chart restriction — is stated at `CertifiedDivisorFamily`, the CHART-TYPED certified family.
14	Its proof never touches the certificate: it consumes `(E i).eqns` and nothing else.  So the
15	statement is stronger than the proof needs, and that mismatch is exactly what blocks the R2
16	port: a widened class over `S i` has no chart-typed certificate at all (that failure IS the
17	content of R2), so the chart-typed assembly cannot be instantiated at widened input, however
18	carrier-free its proof happens to be.
19	
20	This file removes the mismatch by restating the assembly at bare local-equation systems
21	`E : ∀ i, (relCurve C (S i)).LocalEquations`, with the pullback regularity that the certificate
22	used to supply carried as an explicit hypothesis (`Scheme.LocalEquations.PullRegular`).  Nothing
23	in the mathematics changes — the pointwise cross unit still goes through the overlap curve, the
24	glued system is still the immersion transport of the chosen chart's equation, and the chart
25	restriction is still the immersion round trip.  What changes is that the input is now the datum
26	the widened carrier actually has.
27	
28	## The evidence for the claim above, since it is the whole reason this file exists
29	
30	Measured over the entire body of `awayGluedEquations`: the only projections of its input `E`
31	that occur are `.eqns` (eight times) and `.cover` — which is `eqns.cover` — seven.  `.adaptation`
32	and `.certified` never appear, the result is a bare `(relCurve C R).LocalEquations`, and `π`
33	occurs zero times.  Its declared input is nonetheless
34	`E : ∀ i, CertifiedDivisorFamily C (S i) π n`.  The same holds of the certified-input core
35	`DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_certified_away_compat`, whose signature names no cover or adaptation
36	type and whose only two occurrences of "chart" are comments about the *base* localization
37	restriction.
38	
39	## Main declarations — WHAT THIS FILE ACTUALLY CONTAINS
40	
41	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.PullRegular` — the `hreg` side-condition of
42	  `Scheme.LocalEquations.pullback`, named so a *family* of them can be quantified over.  The
43	  naming is necessary rather than cosmetic: the overlap compatibility below has to quantify over
44	  one `hreg` per index, and the anonymous `∀ y z hz, …` spelling cannot be so quantified.
45	  `pullback` does not depend on *which* proof is supplied (`regular` is a `Prop`), so naming the
46	  predicate costs nothing.
47	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.pullRegular_of_isOpenImmersion` — the discharge in the case every away
48	  localization is in.
49	* `AwayCompatPullDivEq` — overlap compatibility at bare systems: over each overlap carrier the two
50	  pulled systems are divisor-equal.  The regularity witnesses are **existentially** bound; see the
51	  declaration's docstring for why the `∀` spelling would be a vacuous obligation.
52	* `germ_awayTransportLoc_mem_nonZeroDivisors` — germ regularity of the immersion transport of a
53	  chart equation.
54	* `exists_res_awayTransportLoc_eq_unit_mul` — the pointwise cross unit, through the overlap curve.
55	* `awayGluedEquationsLoc` — **the glued system** at bare input.
56	* `divEq_pullback_awayGluedEquationsLoc` — **chart restriction**: the pullback of the glue along
57	  `relCurveMap C R (S i)` is divisor-equal to the `i`-th system.
58	* `CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.isLocallyCertifiedAff`, `CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.toZarAff` — a
59	  widened global certificate is a widened local one, so a widened certified family names a class.
60	* `DivFamZarAff.exists_glue_of_certified_away_compat` — **the widened certified-input gluing
61	  core**: compatible WIDENED certified families over a finite away cover of `R` glue to a widened
62	  locally certified class restricting to them.
63	
64	The pinned widened keystone `DivFamZarAff.exists_glue_of_away_compat` is
65	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffGlueZar`.
66	-/

variable (C π n)

/-- **The locally certified divisor functor at an arbitrary test object**
(`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §6 on the Addendum-2 carrier; the `divFam` vehicle):
compatible families of locally certified divisor classes over the affine opens of
`T.left` — the value at a smaller affine open is the base change of the value at a
larger one along the section-restriction algebra map.  On affine tests this is
`DivFamZar` itself (`divFamZarAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its canonical
Zariski-continuous extension. -/
def divFamZar (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
  {s : Π U : T.left.affineOpens, DivFamZar C Γ(T.left, U.1) π n //
    ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}

namespace divFamZar

variable {C π n} {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}

/-- The compatibility of a section of `divFamZar` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/
lemma compat (s : divFamZar C π n T) (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
  s.2 U V h

lemma eval_apply (U : T.left.affineOpens) (s : divFamZar C π n T) :

/-!
# Functoriality of the locally certified divisor vehicle (DD-2 stage S6a)

The locally certified vehicle `divFamZar`
(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarVehicle`) is functorial along an
*arbitrary* morphism `f : T' ⟶ T` of test objects: the value of the restricted family
at an affine open `W ⊆ T'.left` — whose `f`-image need not lie in any affine open of
`T.left` — is *glued* over a finite basic-open refinement of `W` subordinate to the
preimages of affine opens, using the S5b Zariski keystones of `DivFamZar` through the
basic-open toolkit (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarMapKit`).  This is the
`picEtMap` pattern (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap`), clause for clause.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZar.IsPullbackValue`: the characterizing property of the
  glued value — on every affine sub-open lying in the preimage of an affine open, it
  restricts to the pullback of the family value there.  Values with this property are
  unique (`pullbackValue_unique`, from Zariski separation) and exist
  (`exists_isPullbackValue`, from Zariski gluing).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZar.map C π n f : divFamZar C π n T → divFamZar C π n T'`

  no-gluing evaluation `divFamZar.mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom` on affine opens lying in a
  preimage.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAffineEquiv_naturality`: the affine comparison

  over affine tests, `divFamZar.map` along `Spec` of an algebra map corresponds to the

here (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §6: the exact functor spelling is co-signed with the

/-- Existence and uniqueness of the glued value. -/
theorem existsUnique_isPullbackValue (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T)
    (W : T'.left.affineOpens) : ∃! v, IsPullbackValue C π n f s W v := by
  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := exists_isPullbackValue f s W
  exact ⟨v, hv, fun v' hv' => pullbackValue_unique hv' hv⟩

/-! ## The functoriality -/

variable (C π n)

/-- The value of the restricted family at an affine open of the source. -/
noncomputable def mapVal (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T)
    (W : T'.left.affineOpens) : DivFamZar C Γ(T'.left, W.1) π n :=
  (existsUnique_isPullbackValue f s W).choose

lemma mapVal_spec (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) :
    IsPullbackValue C π n f s W (mapVal C π n f s W) :=
  (existsUnique_isPullbackValue f s W).choose_spec.1

lemma mapVal_eq_of (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T) {W : T'.left.affineOpens}
    {v : DivFamZar C Γ(T'.left, W.1) π n} (hv : IsPullbackValue C π n f s W v) :
    mapVal C π n f s W = v :=
  pullbackValue_unique (mapVal_spec C π n f s W) hv

/-- The value of the restricted family on an affine open lying in the preimage of an
affine open is the plain pullback — no gluing. -/
lemma mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T)
    {W : T'.left.affineOpens} {V : T.left.affineOpens} (hV : W.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) :
    mapVal C π n f s W
      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.appLEAlgHom f V.1 W.1 hV) (s.1 V) := by
  have h := mapVal_spec C π n f s W W le_rfl V hV
  rwa [Over.resAlgHom_rfl, DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id] at h

/-- **Restriction of the locally certified vehicle along an arbitrary morphism of test
objects** (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §6 on the Addendum-2 carrier; the `picEtMap`
pattern): the value at each affine open of the source is the glued pullback value. -/
noncomputable def map (f : T' ⟶ T) : divFamZar C π n T → divFamZar C π n T' :=
  fun s =>
    ⟨fun W => mapVal C π n f s W, by
      intro U V h
      beta_reduce
      refine (mapVal_eq_of C π n f s (W := U) ?_).symm
      intro W₀ hW₀ V' hV'
      rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, Over.resAlgHom_comp]
      exact mapVal_spec C π n f s V W₀ (hW₀.trans h) V' hV'⟩

@[simp]
lemma map_val (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) :
    (map C π n f s).1 W = mapVal C π n f s W :=
  rfl

/-- The functor law: restriction along the identity is the identity. -/
theorem map_id (s : divFamZar C π n T) : map C π n (𝟙 T) s = s := by
  refine ext fun W => ?_
  rw [map_val]
  refine mapVal_eq_of C π n (𝟙 T) s ?_
  intro W₀ hW₀ V hV
  have hV' : W₀.1 ≤ V.1 := by
    intro p hp
    have hmem := hV hp
    rw [Over.id_left] at hmem
    exact hmem
  rw [Over.appLEAlgHom_id T V.1 W₀.1 hV hV', s.compat W₀ W hW₀, s.compat W₀ V hV']

/-- The functor law: restriction along a composite is the composite of the
restrictions. -/
theorem map_comp (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T'' ⟶ T') (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
    map C π n (g ≫ f) s = map C π n g (map C π n f s) := by
  classical
  refine ext fun W => ?_

    x = y := by
